# herdr 0.9.5 and herdr-core 0.1.14 violation ledger

Every violation found in herdr 0.9.5 and herdr-core 0.1.14 against the AI-slop and programming rule sources, plus live runtime behavior, so ovis-terminal is designed and reviewed against each one. Severity is copied from the audits; inherit-risk yes means the pattern would carry into ovis-terminal if copied.

## Summary

Ledger of 5174 rows: 5154 source rows from the two herdr-audit aggregates plus 20 runtime rows from the isolated smoke runs. 4074 rows (78%) are marked inherit-risk yes: the pattern would carry into ovis-terminal if its code or protocol were copied.

| by severity | rows |
|---|---:|
| high | 611 |
| medium | 3306 |
| low | 1254 |
| info | 3 |
| **total** | **5174** |

| by source | rows | severity split |
|---|---:|---|
| herdr 0.9.5 (source) | 3894 | high 409, medium 2556, low 929 |
| herdr-core 0.1.14 (source) | 1260 | high 195, medium 744, low 321 |
| runtime (live smoke, 8 hc + 12 herdr) | 20 | high 7, medium 6, low 4, info 3 |

Rules with the most rows:

1. SLOP-7 - 427 rows (298 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
2. PROG-A3 - 402 rows (369 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
3. SLOP-3 - 395 rows (287 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
4. PROG-IRON-cast - 377 rows (259 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
5. PROG-IRON-error - 376 rows (367 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
6. PROG-SMELL-2 - 312 rows (254 inherit-risk yes, highest medium)
7. SLOP-10 - 242 rows (172 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
8. PROG-A1 - 224 rows (212 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
9. RUST-HR-1 - 223 rows (214 inherit-risk yes, highest high)
10. SLOP-2 - 217 rows (190 inherit-risk yes, highest high)

What ovis-terminal must do differently. Duplication (SLOP-7) and primitive obsession (PROG-A3) lead the ledger, so ovis-terminal defines one constant or helper per literal and newtypes for every pane id, terminal id, workspace id, machine name and path before any handler code is written. Errors are the next cluster: string error kinds (PROG-IRON-error), collapsed failure causes (SLOP-2) and dropped errors (RUST-HR-1) all mean ovis-terminal ships one typed error enum per boundary whose stable kind, message and hint reach the client the way hc already does (RT-HC-06) and herdr does not (RT-HD-07, RT-HD-12). Long functions and files (SLOP-3, SLOP-10, PROG-SMELL-1, PROG-SMELL-2) are enforced mechanically: a 250 pure-LOC file cap and a three-parameter cap checked in CI, not left to review. Numeric `as` casts (PROG-IRON-cast, RUST-HR-9) are denied by clippy `as_conversions`, together with unwrap_used, expect_used and a reason-carrying `#[expect]` policy, in a workspace `[lints]` table with a pinned toolchain and deny.toml, which neither upstream has in full. Unsafe stays in one small FFI module with a SAFETY comment per block; herdr has 451 unsafe occurrences against 54 SAFETY comments. Logging goes through tracing with structured fields only, never eprintln in library code (351 non-test eprintln calls in herdr). The runtime rows set protocol requirements the source rows cannot: one target parameter shape with unknown fields rejected (RT-HD-02, RT-HD-03), a multiplexed connection instead of one request per socket (RT-HD-01), idempotent and acknowledged subscriptions (RT-HD-08), and waits that take a cursor so output printed during a send is not lost (RT-HC-02). An explicit agent report must outrank screen heuristics (RT-HD-09), and success output must describe what was verified on the process, not what the status field says (RT-HC-03). Read-only queries must never start daemons (RT-HC-04), and send must not block for seconds by default (RT-HC-01). The keepers section lists what to copy unchanged, most importantly the RAII child slot with Drop teardown, bounded frames checked before allocation, and validation before any side effect.

|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| SLOP-7 | 427 | 298 | high | One named constant or helper per literal/logic block; duplicates are a review failure. |
| PROG-A3 | 402 | 369 | high | Newtypes for names, ids, addresses and paths so invalid cross-use does not compile. |
| SLOP-3 | 395 | 287 | high | Functions stay short and single-purpose; dispatch, validation, I/O and persistence live in separate functions. |
| PROG-IRON-cast | 377 | 259 | high | No `as` numeric casts; use try_from/From or a named checked/saturating helper. |
| PROG-IRON-error | 376 | 367 | high | Typed error enums with stable kinds (thiserror); no string kinds or String errors. |
| PROG-SMELL-2 | 312 | 254 | medium | At most three parameters and no boolean mode flags; use an options struct or an enum. |
| SLOP-10 | 242 | 172 | high | Split files at 250 pure LOC along a responsibility seam. |
| PROG-A1 | 224 | 212 | high | Closed sets are enums end to end, including at the API boundary. |

## Source violations

All 5154 rows of both aggregates, copied verbatim (rule, severity, location, evidence, why, inherit-risk); the original id is appended to the why cell as `[src: V-audit-...]`. ## Patterns worth keeping

Merged from both aggregates (597 entries after merging the two titles that appeared twice: "Structured tracing fields" and "Why-comments"). Each ends with its source audit.

- **RAII slot plus Drop teardown for child processes** (exec.rs:29-57, exec.rs:323-331): `Slot` gives back its place on drop, and `Tree::drop` ends the process group and sweeps the token even if the caller goes away. This is RUST-HR-5 done right; ovis-terminal's PTY/child manager should copy it. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Notified::enable() before re-checking state** (exec.rs:227-237, `stopping()`): registers for the wakeup first, then checks the flag, so no wakeup is lost. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Validate before any side effect** (exec.rs:59-65 `timeout()`, api.rs:409 "checked before anything is typed", exec.rs:134-143): inputs are bounded (timeout, base64, MAX_STDIN) before tokens, files or processes exist. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Bounded frames, checked before allocation** (holder_proto.rs:10 and 138): `MAX_PAYLOAD` is enforced before `vec![0; len]`, and the frame layout is documented in the module header (holder_proto.rs:1-3). [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Only NotFound means "empty"** (paths.rs:59-68 and its test at paths.rs:98-109; config.rs:52-58): a missing state file yields the default, while an unreadable or corrupt one is an error, never silently replaced. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **One method table drives schema, CLI coverage and docs** (api.rs:31-35 and 55-151, with the guard test at cli.rs:930-942): an OpenRPC document is generated from the table and a test fails if a method has no command and is not marked API-only. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Slow subscribers get `missed` plus a fresh snapshot, not a backlog** (events.rs:1-2, 13-14, 157-164): a bounded mpsc with `try_send` and a `behind` flag keeps memory bounded and tells the consumer to resync. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Per-terminal input serialization with a human-typing gate** (input.rs:21-53, 111-112, 134-151): agent input and a person's keystrokes never interleave. Pair it with the scope-guard fix noted in V-audit-core-src-1 rows for input.rs:131. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Exhaustive match on an owned enum** (api.rs:513-518 over `Interrupted`, notes.rs:12-19 `Job`, events.rs:147-166 and 181-199 over `Sink`): the compiler proves every variant is handled (only events.rs:89 uses a wildcard). [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Async handlers push blocking file I/O onto spawn_blocking** (api.rs:462, 467, 472, 475-477): `blocking()` is the single place that does it. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Bounds-checked binary parsing returning Option, tested against the real binary** (client.rs:126-153 with the test at client.rs:155-165): every offset uses `get`/`checked_add`, with no panics on malformed input. (Still hand-rolled per RUST-HR-6, but a good model if one must be.) [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Atomic replace that cleans up on every error path and keeps file mode** (files.rs:154-180) and **all-or-none, exactly-once edit semantics** (files.rs:94-125 with test files.rs:190-204). [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Boundary validation against option injection** (machines.rs:108-122 `check_target` rejects a leading `-`, whitespace and control characters; test at machines.rs:551-553). [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Errors that carry a hint** (`RpcError::new(kind, message, hint)` used at addr.rs:38-42, paths.rs:40-46, files.rs:42): agent-readable remediation is part of the error shape. Keep the hint, but make the kind an enum. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Safety comment where unsafe is unavoidable** (cli.rs:507-508 states why no other thread exists yet). It is still missing a Miri proof, see its row. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Reading keys through the program's real terminal modes** (keys.rs:48-71) and **a tiny `main`** that only calls `cli::main()` (main.rs:1-3). [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Tests named as sentences with messages on each assertion** (addr.rs:52, kept.rs:118, attach.rs:353-433, files.rs:191-217): they assert behavior and fail with context. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- **Cow to avoid allocation when no rewrite is needed** (attach.rs:92-107 `shown`), in line with RUST-HR-3. [audit-core-src-1.md]
- Single method table: `methods!` in herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/rpc.rs:167 generates `METHOD_NAMES`, `discover()` and `dispatch()` from one list, so the schema, hello method list and dispatch cannot drift apart. Adopt it, with typed params and results as it already does. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Cancel-on-drop guards: `Asked` in herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/remote.rs:131-142 sends `$/cancelRequest` if a call is given up, `Execs` in herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/server.rs:359-367 aborts running execs when the connection closes, and `Scratch` in herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/releases.rs:134 removes the download dir on every path (RUST-HR-5 done right). [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Per-call deadline and fail-fast on line loss: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/remote.rs:73-125 bounds every remote call and fails pending calls the moment the line drops (line 415) rather than waiting for the deadline. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Lost-wakeup-safe waiting: create `notified()`, `enable()` it, then check the condition, as in herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/runtime.rs:658-671 and herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/wait.rs:145-147. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Bounded parsing of untrusted terminal output: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/relay.rs:12-14 caps CSI and string length and passes overlong input through unexamined, and the tests at relay.rs:156-189 feed the same input whole and byte by byte. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Race-free file staging with sanitised names: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/put.rs:41-68 uses `create_new` with a collision counter and a `clean()` that strips directories and dots, and the test at put.rs:82-83 pins traversal inputs. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Checked id arithmetic: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/terminals.rs:187-200 `parse_id` uses checked_mul/checked_add and returns None on overflow, `create` at terminals.rs:247 turns id exhaustion into a typed error, and the tests at terminals.rs:524-542 cover `u32::MAX` and never-reused ids. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Crash-ordered state change: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/server.rs:99-122 removes the copied machine's state before writing the new identity so a crash retries, and the test at server.rs:427 covers it. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Non-blocking writer thread per holder: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/runtime.rs:95-100 and 332-340 queue frames to a writer thread so the core never blocks on a socket while holding its lock (the comment names the deadlock it avoids). [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Escalating, rescanning process cleanup: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/sweep.rs:71-92 goes HUP, TERM, KILL and re-looks before each step, and sweep.rs:1-4 states the accepted escape hatch. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Backpressure by credit with repaint on overflow: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/viewers.rs:111-130 collects connections whose queue overflowed and repaints them once, instead of buffering without bound. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Pure merge function with behavior-named regression tests: `merge_up` at herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/stitch.rs:110 returns an enum and has 12 tests at stitch.rs:439-617; herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/status.rs:173-189 tests turn counting by behavior. [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Stable public vs. internal split intent: herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/terminals.rs:417-447 keeps core bookkeeping out of API results (adopt the intent, but implement it with two structs, see the PRIVATE finding). [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Hygiene baseline: zero `#[allow]` across all 15 files, and most `let _ =` discards are channel sends where the receiver may legitimately be gone (the exceptions are listed in the table). [audit-core-src-2.md]
- Explicit resource bounds as named constants with documented intent (wire.rs:24-28, `WINDOW`, `MAX_PENDING`, `MAX_CONTROL`), and the payload cap checked at the decode boundary before use (wire.rs:42-45). ovis-terminal should keep slow-reader backpressure explicit. [audit-core-src-3.md]
- Credit-based flow control with control frames prioritized over streams and round-robin fairness (wire.rs:233-252, doc at 153-155), so one stalled viewer cannot block typing or replies. [audit-core-src-3.md]
- Deciding code separate from IO: `Outbox` is a pure state machine with no tokio dependency, exercised by synchronous tests (wire.rs:254-353); this matches the repo's "deciding code stays separate from IO" rule. [audit-core-src-3.md]
- Behavior-named tests that can fail, e.g. a_program_that_ends_still_delivers_its_last_output_first (wire.rs:283) and a_line_stream_that_falls_behind_still_delivers_whole_lines (wire.rs:300). [audit-core-src-3.md]
- Whole-line overflow handling for event streams (wire.rs:212-221) so a repaint never starts mid-line. [audit-core-src-3.md]
- `saturating_add` for credit (wire.rs:229) and doc comments that state the why on constants and state fields; no unsafe, no #[allow], no logging side channels. [audit-core-src-3.md]
- Lock access funneled through one `outbox()` accessor and one `with()` that wakes after unlocking (wire.rs:125-143), though the poison policy needs documenting (row 013). [audit-core-src-3.md]
- **RAII guard for cleanup on every path (RUST-HR-5).** `Watching` decrements the waiting counter in `Drop`, so early returns and cancelled futures cannot leak it (crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs:40-57). [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Task-scoped fan-out with cancel-on-drop (RUST-ASYNC-cancel).** `JoinSet` owns the local and remote waits, and returning early drops it, which aborts the rest (crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs:146-186). [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Std mutex never held across an await (RUST-ASYNC-mutex).** State is locked in a block and released before the await (crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs:121-164, crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs:253-256). [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Optimistic concurrency with a version and a recovery hint (crates/herdr-core/src/api/doc.rs:15-22).** The conflict error tells the caller to read doc.get and retry; the version uses `checked_add` rather than wrapping (crates/herdr-core/src/api/doc.rs:23). [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Errors carry a code, a message and a next-step hint (crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs:78, crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs:121).** Agent-friendly and worth copying, once the code becomes a typed enum. [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Size limits and non-finite input are rejected before work starts (crates/herdr-core/src/api/types.rs:82-96, crates/herdr-core/src/api/doc.rs:11).** `Duration::try_from_secs_f64` and `is_finite` stop NaN at the boundary. [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Exhaustive tuple match for status reason (crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs:94-98).** No wildcard arm. [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Truncation that respects char boundaries (crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs:63-67),** with a regression test (crates/herdr-core/src/api/run.rs:239-245). [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Atomic file persistence helper used for state (crates/herdr-core/src/api/doc.rs:2, 26).** [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Workspace lints, deny.toml and a pinned layout exist (RUST-CARGO-lints/deny).** crates/herdr-core/Cargo.toml has [lints] and the repo root has deny.toml; no #[allow] and no unsafe appear in these four files. [audit-core-src-api.md]
- **Doc comments explain why, not what (crates/herdr-core/src/api/waiting.rs:22-23, 39-40, 128-130).** They are the opposite of SLOP-1. [audit-core-src-api.md]
- Staged, verified binary swap: `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/cli/update.rs:71-77` copies beside the target, runs the verification callback on the staged file, then swaps, so a half-written hc never exists (`// Staged beside it, checked, then swapped in`). Adopt for any self-update or runtime-binary replacement. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Refuse-with-hint errors: `update.rs:68-69` (`--force to go back anyway`) and `file.rs:20` (`pipe it in: hc ... < file`) give every failure a kind, a message and a next action, which suits agent callers. Keep the shape, make the kind a typed enum. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Bounded input reads: `file.rs:22-26` reads at most max+1 bytes and rejects the excess, so a huge pipe cannot exhaust memory. Keep the idea (fix the cast). [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- TTY gating before interactive prompts: `machine.rs:24-26` requires both stdin and stderr to be terminals, and `machine.rs:88-94` refuses login without one, so an agent never hangs on a password prompt. Keep. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Explicit consent with a non-interactive override: `machine.rs:47-61` prompts only at a terminal and honors `p.install` otherwise, an agent-native install flow. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- All-or-none edit semantics stated at the CLI surface (`file.rs:12`) and validated before the RPC call (`file.rs:67-69`). [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Agent-facing projection: `output.rs:141-155` (`short`) returns a compact fact record and points to `hc get` for the full one, which keeps agent context small. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Shell-faithful exec exit codes: `output.rs:285-293` maps timeout to 124, signals to 128+n and passes stdout/stderr bytes through untouched. Keep the convention, fix the casts. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Fail-safe version comparison: `update.rs:23` ("anything unparsed is not older") is documented and tested (cli.rs:990-991). [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Why-comments rather than what-comments: `output.rs:52`, `output.rs:149`, `update.rs:31-32` explain intent and edge cases; there are no obvious-restating comments (SLOP-1) in any of the four files. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Existing tests cover the highest-churn logic: picker ordering, item layout, `describe_wait` and `older` in cli.rs:866-991. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Supply-chain hygiene is present: `herdr-core/deny.toml` exists (RUST-CARGO-deny satisfied), and the crate opts into workspace lints. [audit-core-src-cli.md]
- Pure decision core with injected clock and an exhaustive match: `observe(intent, event, now_ns)` matches every Event variant with no wildcard and is unit-tested separately from IO (macos_shutdown.rs:29, test macos_shutdown.rs:198). Rules: PROG-A4, RUST-HR-7, SLOP-9. [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Pure argument builders separated from process launch and tested for secrets and expansion: `unit_args`, `environment_file`, `service_env` (systemd.rs:235, systemd.rs:179, systemd.rs:214); tests at systemd.rs:356 assert no secret reaches argv. [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Secrets-safe environment hand-off: private 0700 directory, create_new 0600 file, removal on write failure (systemd.rs:197), with a test checking modes (systemd.rs:443). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- RAII for terminal state: `RawMode` restores termios or console modes in Drop on every exit path (unix.rs:397, windows.rs:1117); signal handlers only set a flag (unix.rs:364). Rule: RUST-HR-5. [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Owned handles for Win32 resources: OwnedHandle for tokens, jobs, snapshots (windows_exec.rs:111, windows.rs:770), and a `check(BOOL) -> io::Result<()>` helper (windows.rs:28). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- The only SAFETY-commented unsafe in the shard: dynamic ConPTY loading with per-start (not per-process) failure and documented fn signatures (windows.rs:716-windows.rs:732). Rule: RUST-HR-2 (still lacks Miri proof). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Pipe security by default: restrictive SDDL DACL plus integrity label, reject remote clients, and SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION on connect (windows.rs:174, windows.rs:223, windows.rs:155). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Reap-race-aware wait: `waitid(WNOWAIT)` leaves the child unreaped so its pgid cannot be recycled, with the reason documented (unix.rs:180). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Transactional binary update: stage, verify with a caller-supplied `works` check, then rename, with explicit rollback and bounded retry (windows.rs:393, windows.rs:504, simpler form unix.rs:149) - keep the design, split the function. [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Same-surface Pty abstraction across OSes (reader/writer/resize/signal/hang_up) so shared code has no cfg (unix.rs:264, windows.rs:766). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Comments state rationale (why), not mechanics; no obvious-comment slop beyond section banners (e.g. systemd.rs:229). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Poison-tolerant locking: `lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` on small state instead of unwrap (macos_shutdown.rs:63, windows.rs:750). Rule: RUST-CONC-lock-poison. [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Typed one-line Drop guard for FFI registrations: Registration::new relies on Drop to cancel already-registered tokens when a later registration fails (macos_shutdown.rs:184). [audit-core-src-platform.md]
- Behavior-named test (`a_remote_missed_invalidates_..._with_the_local_sequence`, tests.rs:7) states the observable contract, not the mechanism. [audit-core-src-remote.md]
- Per-process-and-random scratch directory (tests.rs:8-12: pid + `random_hex()`) isolates parallel runs; the test constructs `Paths` explicitly, so it never touches the real core. [audit-core-src-remote.md]
- Real `Core::start` plus real channel sinks (tests.rs:20, 33-40) test the event fan-out without mocks, in line with "few end-to-end tests over many mocks". [audit-core-src-remote.md]
- Positive plus negative assertions on both an unfiltered and a filtered subscriber (tests.rs:46-50) check the filter scoping, and the local sequence (7) differs from the remote one (9999), so a pass-through bug would fail. [audit-core-src-remote.md]
- Lock scope is limited to a block (tests.rs:33-41), so the state lock is not held while the test goes on. [audit-core-src-remote.md]

- **Socket hardening and ownership-checked cleanup.** 0o600 permissions (server.rs:29, 304), `SocketFileIdentity` so Drop only removes the socket this process created (server.rs:44-60), and cleanup on the spawn-failure path (server.rs:153-160) with a why-comment. [audit-herdr-api-2.md]

- **Cursor-based event history with explicit loss reporting.** `EventHistoryError::{Lost, Unavailable}` mapped to `events_lost` (subscriptions.rs:326-340) tells a slow client to resync rather than dropping events silently; tests pin this (subscription_socket_tests.rs:272-304). Adopt as a general atomic-config-write primitive (but as a type, not per-agent). [audit-herdr-integration-2.md]
- Best-effort cleanup logged with structured fields rather than eprintln: `tracing::warn!(path = %path.display(), %err, ...)` at targets.rs:1140 (follows LOG-unstructured/LOG-practice). [audit-herdr-integration-2.md]
- Uninstall that attempts every step and aggregates errors instead of aborting on first: targets.rs:847-880 (`uninstall_opencode`), once typed. [audit-herdr-integration-2.md]
- Herdr-owned file isolation: owning a dedicated config file and never editing the user's other hooks (targets.rs:1741-1743 Grok comment; antigravity block rewrite near line 1618) keeps uninstall a straight delete. [audit-herdr-integration-2.md]
- Idempotent writes: compare new vs existing content and only write on change (targets.rs:150-158, 214-218). [audit-herdr-integration-2.md]
- Preflight `check_config_targets` before any mutation (targets.rs:126, 162) and platform split with cfg isolated to small helpers (targets.rs:1477-1486). [audit-herdr-integration-2.md]

- Table-driven cross-target invariants: `bundled_integration_asset_versions_match_expected_versions` iterates every (name, asset, version) tuple (tests.rs:3736-3739), catching drift in one test instead of N copies. [audit-herdr-integration-3.md]
- Behavioural test names state the contract (`install_claude_is_idempotent_for_hook_entries` tests.rs:1009; `install_omp_refuses_shared_pi_extension_directory` tests.rs:713) and cover idempotence, legacy migration and preserve-user-config paths (SLOP-9 satisfied). [audit-herdr-integration-3.md]
- Version probing degrades gracefully: missing/unparseable agent version yields a warning and install proceeds, only a confirmed too-old version errors (doc comment version.rs:43-45), with one test per outcome (tests.rs:87-130). [audit-herdr-integration-3.md]
- Comments explain why and cite an issue (tests.rs:1188-1192 "See #5253"); no SLOP-1 hits. [audit-herdr-integration-3.md]
- types.rs has no unsafe, no #[allow], no unwrap; `IntegrationStatusKind` (types.rs:161) is a Copy enum and `needs_install` (types.rs:189) matches states without a wildcard (PROG-A4, RUST-HR-7). [audit-herdr-integration-3.md]
- Hook tests execute the shipped shell/PowerShell hook with a fake herdr binary and piped stdin (tests.rs:4292), testing the real surface instead of mocks. [audit-herdr-integration-3.md]

- Typed process identity: `AgentProcess { pid, start_token }` defends against pid reuse and the four-way `AgentJobStatus` enum replaces bool flags (herdr/src/pane/background_agent.rs:13, :27). Adopt the pid + start-token pairing, but newtype the ints. [audit-herdr-pane-1.md]
- Module-level doc comments explain the why (job control vs exit) and per-field invariants (herdr/src/pane/background_agent.rs:1, herdr/src/pane/cursor.rs:101). [audit-herdr-pane-1.md]
- Pure decision functions that take explicit inputs and a clock (`now: Instant`), so timing logic is deterministic and testable without sleeps (herdr/src/pane/cursor.rs:111, herdr/src/pane/agent_detection.rs:39). [audit-herdr-pane-1.md]
- Closure injection for OS probes (`live_group`, `start_token`) keeps process queries out of the state logic (herdr/src/pane/background_agent.rs:55). [audit-herdr-pane-1.md]

- Zero `unsafe` and zero non-test `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in all 7 files; fallible conversions use `Option`/`?` and `try_from` (herdr/src/pane/input.rs:264). [audit-herdr-pane-1.md]
- Typed `TerminalId` rather than a bare string for pane/terminal identity (herdr/src/pane/state.rs:7). [audit-herdr-pane-1.md]

- Zero `unsafe`, zero `unwrap()`/`expect()`, zero `#[allow]` outside tests across 3161 non-test lines (herdr/src/pane/terminal.rs, whole non-test region). This is the bar ovis-terminal should hold. [audit-herdr-pane-2.md]
- Structured `tracing` fields instead of formatted strings, for example `debug!(pane = pane_id.raw(), owner_pgid, "tracked transient default color override")` (herdr/src/pane/terminal.rs:1383) and `error!(pane = pane_id.raw(), "ghostty core lock poisoned in reader")` at :1362. Poison is logged at the decision point here, which is the model for the silent sites. [audit-herdr-pane-2.md]

- Dirty-state discipline: nothing is mutated until every row is collected, then dirty is cleared, with a Fallback outcome as the safe path (herdr/src/pane/terminal.rs:2751, :2617). - Typed Result with a named error type and `?` propagation in visible_render_lines (herdr/src/pane/terminal/windows_recent_fallback.rs:160-186). [audit-herdr-pane-3.md]

- Manual symlink resolution so a write lands on a dangling stow-style target (herdr/src/persist/io.rs:19-43 and plugin_registry.rs:36-58). The plugin_registry version errors on a loop (:57), which is the better behavior. [audit-herdr-persist.md]
- Never clobber state the process did not load: SessionWriter.protect_unloaded keeps a recovery copy before the first save (herdr/src/persist/writer.rs:9-27, :122-124). Rename it positively. [audit-herdr-persist.md]
- Recovery copies are published via pending file, rename, and directory fsync, and older copies are pruned only after the new one is durable (herdr/src/persist/writer.rs:188-219, :235-237); timestamps stay monotonic if the clock moves backwards (:143-151). [audit-herdr-persist.md]
- Newer-version files are ignored with a structured warning rather than overwritten (herdr/src/persist/io.rs:116-125, writer.rs:105). [audit-herdr-persist.md]
- Structured load logging with event, subsystem, outcome, and path fields (herdr/src/persist/io.rs:99-101, :106-109, :118-122). [audit-herdr-persist.md]
- Closure-scoped lock with RAII release and a strict-read vs lenient-load split: `update` and `read` use strict reads under the lock, `load` degrades to empty (herdr/src/persist/plugin_registry.rs:19-34, :80-112). [audit-herdr-persist.md]
- Legacy migration through a Raw type and `From<LegacyWorkspaceSnapshot>` (herdr/src/persist/snapshot.rs:155-180, :182-228), with the migration kept separate from the current model. [audit-herdr-persist.md]

- Pure, exhaustive recursive tree functions: prune_restored_node, remap_inner, collect_ids_inner (herdr/src/persist/restore.rs:923-946, :968-995, :1003-1011); no wildcard arms on Node or LayoutSnapshot. [audit-herdr-persist.md]

- Overflow awareness where it was applied: checked_add and saturating_sub (herdr/src/persist/restore.rs:336, :360, :433; writer.rs:148, :237). [audit-herdr-persist.md]

- Hygiene baseline: no unsafe, no #[allow], no numeric `as` casts, no unwrap/expect in non-test code across 5191 lines. [audit-herdr-persist.md]

- Hard bounds on external I/O: clipboard.rs:8 (`TIMEOUT`), :42 and :75 (deadline checks) and :105 (`FileTooLarge` cap); linux.rs:37-58 names scan limits (`CHILD_GROUPS_SCAN_LIMIT`, `FOREGROUND_TREE_SCAN_LIMIT`, byte and pid limits) instead of reading /proc unbounded. [audit-herdr-platform-1.md]

- Private-by-construction state files: linux.rs:133-143 (`create_new` with mode 0600), :145-172 (copy ownership and xattrs/ACLs onto the empty temporary before writing secrets) and macos.rs:63-100 (non-inheriting ACL supplied at creation rather than cleared later). [audit-herdr-platform-1.md]
- Exhaustive match on a controlled enum with no wildcard arm: linux.rs:827-831 and macos.rs:1181-1185 (`Signal`). [audit-herdr-platform-1.md]
- Structured logging and bounded reconnect: power.rs:18 `tracing::debug!(%error, ...)`, shutdown.rs:19 with `retry_seconds` field, backoff capped at 60 s (power.rs:21). [audit-herdr-platform-1.md]
- Explicit atomic orderings (Release store / Acquire load) at shutdown.rs:67, power.rs:111,164 (RUST-CONC-ordering). [audit-herdr-platform-1.md]

- **Lock poison recovery without unwrap**: `HostShutdownIntentCell::lock` uses `unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)` on a plain Copy value (herdr/src/platform/mod.rs:121). All nine files have zero unwrap/expect outside test code. [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Pure decision logic separated from OS glue**: `observe` takes the intent, an event and a timestamp and returns a bool, with an exhaustive match over `LoginwindowEvent` and no wildcard (herdr/src/platform/macos/shutdown.rs:57); the event table is a const (herdr/src/platform/macos/shutdown.rs:42). Same shape in `stale_job_labels` (herdr/src/platform/macos/launchd_spawn.rs:166). [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Cancellation by ownership**: monitors abort their task on Drop (herdr/src/platform/mod.rs:50), and the bridge watchdog stops when its `_stop` Sender drops (herdr/src/platform/remote_bridge.rs:25) with `fetch_max` on an atomic and a suspend-inclusive clock (herdr/src/platform/remote_bridge.rs:53). - **SAFETY comments that state the invariant**: herdr/src/platform/unix_image_files.rs:222 and herdr/src/platform/macos/shutdown.rs:194 name the exact invariant relied on. [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Private-path hardening**: directories opened with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC then uid and mode checked on the fd (herdr/src/platform/unix_image_files.rs:209); files created with create_new and mode 0o600 (herdr/src/platform/macos/launchd_spawn.rs:119); never recursive delete of unknown content (herdr/src/platform/unix_image_files.rs:183). - **Identity-pinned filesystem state**: SSH agent publication re-checks the dev/inode before every write and in Drop (herdr/src/platform/ssh_agent.rs:149, herdr/src/platform/ssh_agent.rs:208); `PinnedSshControlSocket` hard-links the inode so a replacement cannot receive stop requests (herdr/src/platform/unix_common.rs:816); publication uses symlink-to-temp then rename (herdr/src/platform/ssh_agent.rs:194). - **Compile-time exhaustiveness on single-variant enums**: `let crate::ipc::LocalStream::UdSocket(stream) = stream;` breaks the build when a variant is added (herdr/src/platform/unix_common.rs:97). `ServerQuitSignal` Display matches with no wildcard (herdr/src/platform/mod.rs:165). [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Checked conversions where they matter**: `i32::try_from(process_id)` in `StatusCommandGuard::new` (herdr/src/platform/unix_common.rs:595) and `checked_add` with an error on sequence exhaustion (herdr/src/platform/unix_image_files.rs:143). [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Resource bounds as named consts**: MAX_FILES, MAX_BYTES, MAX_GENERATIONS, STALE_GRACE (herdr/src/platform/unix_image_files.rs:10). [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Test seams without global state**: `refresh_at(now)` takes an injected Instant (herdr/src/platform/ssh_agent.rs:223). [audit-herdr-platform-2.md]
- **Typed handle ownership.** `OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle` right after a successful OS call (windows.rs:192, :234, :1036) gives RAII cleanup on every path (RUST-HR-5). [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]
- **Safe conversions in places.** `usize::try_from` / `u8::try_from` are used on the time-conversion path (:825, :1125). Casts elsewhere should follow this. [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]
- **Documented unsafe where it exists.** Several FFI calls carry a SAFETY comment that names the pointer and length contract (:2615-2616, :1616, :1644). ovis-terminal should make that a lint, not a habit. [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]
- **Explanatory WHY comments.** Examples: the usize storage that keeps TOKEN_USER aligned (:240), and the Korean-only IME toggle rationale (:3240-3244). They explain a non-obvious constraint, not the code. [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]

- **Poison recovery is deliberate.** Locks use `unwrap_or_else(|err| err.into_inner())` instead of `unwrap` (:1817), so there is no panic on shared state. ovis-terminal should keep the no-panic intent but centralize it in one helper that logs the poison. [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]
- **Cache identity checks.** Cached foreground selections are validated by process creation time (:2140), which guards against pid reuse. The same idea should back any typed Pid. [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]
- **Zero unwrap/expect in non-test code.** Errors propagate with `?` and `io::Result`. [audit-herdr-platform-3.md]

RUST-HR-5. [audit-herdr-platform-4.md]

- Frozen wire tags enforced by tests (client_message_wire_tags_reflect_current_order, herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:1957) and append-only extensible EndpointControl variant (herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:616). [audit-herdr-protocol-2.md]
- Forged-length protection for graphics bytes via a bytes visitor (herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:1231-1233) with a legacy-wire-compatibility test at 1778. [audit-herdr-protocol-2.md]
- Exhaustive matches for ClientKeyKind and ClientKeyCode::to_crossterm (herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:206-210, 242-261); `#[serde(other)]` forward-compat for unknown command actions (herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:976). [audit-herdr-protocol-2.md]
- Zero unsafe, zero #[allow], zero panics outside tests; extensive roundtrip, oversized, truncated and malformed frame tests (starting herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:1871). [audit-herdr-protocol-2.md]
- **Typed fd ownership at the struct boundary.** `WakePipe` holds `OwnedFd` and an `Arc<OwnedFd>` writer, so close-on-drop is automatic (herdr/src/pty/fd.rs:53-55, 80-83), and `create_wake_pipe` wraps raw fds in `OwnedFd` before any fallible step so `?` cannot leak them (fd.rs:92-96). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Cleanup on the error path.** `duplicate_cloexec_fd` closes the dup if set_cloexec fails (fd.rs:44-47). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Self-pipe wake with EINTR/EAGAIN handling.** `WakeWriter::wake` treats WouldBlock as success and retries on Interrupted (fd.rs:59-76); `drain_wake_fd` mirrors it (fd.rs:107-126). Nonblocking and cloexec are set on both ends (fd.rs:94-96). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **EINTR-aware poll with a recomputed deadline** rather than restarting the full timeout (fd.rs:166-194), and POLLNVAL/POLLERR surfaced as errors (fd.rs:198-209). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Saturating geometry conversion** for ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel (fd.rs:230-235), correct in intent even though it uses `as`. [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Single-owner actor with explicit state enum.** `ActorState { Running, Quiesced, Released }` (actor/unix.rs:22-27) is matched exhaustively in the control paths, and the SubmissionPhase/Boundary split models the prompt-then-Enter protocol as a state machine (unix.rs:468-491). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Backpressure and wake discipline.** Bounded command channel (unix.rs:19, 393), `try_send` mapped to WouldBlock/BrokenPipe (unix.rs:172-179), and every handle method wakes the actor, documented in the comment at unix.rs:15-17. [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Two-phase handoff with rollback/release** (begin_handoff, rollback_handoff, release_after_commit; unix.rs:250-357) is a good template for process-upgrade fd transfer, aside from the swallowed rollback result flagged above. [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Structured tracing fields** (`debug!(pane = self.pane_id, err = %err, ...)`, unix.rs:551, 574, 830) rather than formatted strings, which is correct LOG-unstructured behavior; only the levels need fixing. [audit-herdr-pty.md] Also: (bootstrap.rs:91-95, 113-125; handoff.rs:119-136): field-style logs with `%err`. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Test coverage of the actor protocol is broad and uses real socketpairs** (unix.rs:1058-1878), including a leak test that counts parent PTY fds (backend/unix.rs:72-93). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- **Dup-then-drop of the portable-pty pair** so only one master fd stays in the parent (backend/unix.rs:26-36). [audit-herdr-pty.md]
- Closed `RemoteKeybindings` enum with exhaustive `match` in `as_str` (args.rs:20-25), no wildcard arm over the enum itself. [audit-herdr-remote-1.md]
- Explicit `--` terminator handling so everything after it passes through untouched (args.rs:50-53). [audit-herdr-remote-1.md]
- Rejection of targets starting with `-` to block option injection into ssh (args.rs:123-125). [audit-herdr-remote-1.md]
- `Vec::with_capacity(args.len())` for the cleaned arg vector (args.rs:38), and `get(index + 1)` with `let ... else` instead of indexing (args.rs:63). [audit-herdr-remote-1.md]
- Cross-flag validation (`--remote-keybindings requires --remote`) done at the parse boundary (args.rs:109-111). [audit-herdr-remote-1.md]
- Zero unwrap/expect/unsafe/#[allow] in non-test code. [audit-herdr-remote-1.md]
- Zero unwrap/expect/panic/unsafe/#[allow] in production code (attach.rs 1-3675): errors propagate with `?` and `io::Error`. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Thread panics are converted to errors on join, not propagated: attach.rs:1264 and the join chain at 3402-3409. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- RAII cleanup on every path: `Drop for SshStdioBridge` (3109) sets stop, removes the socket only if owned (`remove_socket_file_if_owned`), then joins the worker; `Drop for ManagedSshConfigDirectory` (739); `OwnedSshChild` guards the child. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Cancellation is explicit and race-tested: `BridgeUploadStop` (3202) uses an atomic flag plus a wake handle with `swap` so cancel fires once (3216); Acquire/Release ordering is used consistently. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Bounded memory for remote-controlled output: `SSH_DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT_LIMIT` and `NONINTERACTIVE_SSH_STDERR_LIMIT` (lines 41-42), plus `wait_with_output_limit`. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Socket hygiene: private listener, mode 0600 constant (33), identity check before unlink (3046). [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Option-injection and quoting treated as first-class, with dedicated tests (`authentication_command_rejects_option_injection`, 4281; quote tests 4631+); `sanitize_path_component` (3661) whitelists characters. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Failure from a background bridge thread is surfaced via a bounded `sync_channel(1)` plus `try_send` (3056, 3070), avoiding a blocked worker. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- Tests cover cancellation, drain-on-exit, large frames and quoting with real streams; this follows the SLOP-9 expectation. [audit-herdr-remote-2.md]
- **Drop-guard cleanup (RUST-HR-5).** `OwnedSshChild` kills and reaps only its own SSH child and says why (a shared multiplex master must survive): herdr/src/remote/process.rs:17-25. `Registration` signals its worker and joins it in Drop: herdr/src/remote/ssh_agent.rs:62-69. `SavedSshBridge` holds the bridge as an RAII guard: herdr/src/remote/saved.rs:11-13. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Scoped threads with explicit cancel/finish control.** `thread::scope` guarantees no leaked I/O threads and `PipeControl` separates `stopped` from `finished`, so output is drained after exit without waiting on inherited descendants: herdr/src/remote/process.rs:27-56 and 177-239. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Acquire/Release on cross-thread flags.** herdr/src/remote/process.rs:43-50. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Bounded output capture that still drains.** `limit + 1` bytes are kept (so truncation is detectable) and the rest is drained to a sink so the child cannot block on a full pipe: herdr/src/remote/process.rs:131-143. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Why-comments on non-obvious decisions.** For example "A rejected command can close stdin early; its SSH error is more useful" (herdr/src/remote/process.rs:230) and "Only this SSH invocation is ours" (herdr/src/remote/process.rs:21). [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Pure decision function with a closed enum result.** `remote_server_restart_reason` returns `RemoteServerRestartReason`, a pure function with one test per branch: herdr/src/remote/restart_policy.rs:1-37, 64-161. The enum is matched without wildcards at the call site. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Structured logging with fields** via `tracing::debug!(%error, ...)`: herdr/src/remote/ssh_agent.rs:29, 106. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Behaviour-focused tests.** They assert descendants survive cleanup, that the child is reaped and that the output is bounded: herdr/src/remote/process.rs:361-467. Test names state the invariant, e.g. `bridge_paths_use_profile_identity_not_target_or_session` (herdr/src/remote/saved.rs:216). [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Zero unsafe, zero non-test unwrap/expect, in all five files.** [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- **Identity-based socket paths with a short fallback** keep bridge sockets stable and unrelated to user-supplied target/session strings: herdr/src/remote/saved.rs:182-187. [audit-herdr-remote-3.md]
- Bounded two-lane writer queue: a control lane that is reliable and prioritized, a single-slot droppable render lane, and sender refcount shutdown via Condvar (herdr/src/server/client_transport.rs:120-127, 273-280, 356-377). Slow clients cannot build lag; ovis-terminal should copy this for PTY output fan-out. [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Explicit wire limits with saturating arithmetic and a typed outcome enum instead of bool/String (herdr/src/server/client_transport.rs:564-637). [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Two-phase endpoint decode: parse only `{id, method}` first so malformed bodies still yield a correlated error (herdr/src/server/client_transport.rs:97-116). [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Typed framing errors matched individually (UnexpectedEof / Oversized / other) with structured log fields and a handshake read timeout (herdr/src/server/client_transport.rs:42, 692-705, 1025-1029). [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Contract snapshot test pinning advertised method names and request shapes (herdr/src/server/client_commands.rs:241-300). [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Response chunking with named byte limits and final_chunk flag, so oversized API replies do not break framing (herdr/src/server/client_commands.rs:10-13, 123-136). [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Explicit Phase enum, named timing constants and deadline fields for the alternate-screen read state machine (herdr/src/server/alt_screen_read.rs:10-22); the consuming `self -> PollOutcome` signature is a type-state-like hand-off. [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Daemon launch: stdio nulled, new session, cwd handed via env, structured `info!` fields (herdr/src/server/autodetect.rs:204-251). [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- Production code has zero unwrap/expect and zero unsafe; `#[allow]` appears once. Test-only helpers are cfg(test) gated. [audit-herdr-server-1.md]
- **Two-phase handoff with explicit rollback** (handoff.rs:115-139, 212-230): cleanup_failed_import_child checks try_wait, then kills and reaps, with a structured `pid`/`status` field on every branch, and wait_owned_ack downgrades a late failure to a warning with a reason. Copy this for any PTY hand-over or upgrade path. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Bounded, deadline-driven socket I/O** (handoff.rs:20-24, 337-358, 377): every wait has a named timeout constant, `Interrupted` is retried, and the line length is capped. Borrow the discipline, but see V rows on SLOP-8 and RUST-ASYNC-block for the cost. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Defensive, documented cmsg parsing** (handoff.rs:489-495, 506-525): the payload is bounded by the header and the kernel-written length, MSG_CTRUNC is treated as unrecoverable, and the fd count is checked against what was expected. The comments state invariants and not mechanics. The fix for ovis is to keep this logic and wrap it in an OwnedFd type with a SAFETY comment. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Batching with a stated reason** (handoff.rs:25-29): FDS_PER_MESSAGE=64 cites the 253/254 kernel limits, so pane count is unbounded. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Backward-compatible persisted manifest with frozen-shape tests** (handoff.rs:45-53, 592-628): `#[serde(default)]` on new fields, plus a test that decodes a manifest into the old struct shape. This is the right way to evolve a state-persistence format, and these tests can fail. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Safe-by-construction file staging** (clipboard_image.rs:6, 27-38, 58-72, 96-111): an extension allowlist that falls back to png, create_new with an atomic retry, 0600 files in a 0700 dir, and age-based cleanup. Adopt it for any client-supplied blob. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Exhaustive enum match** (clients.rs:359-365, headless.rs:2657): the last arms list their variants explicitly, and ServerEvent dispatch has no wildcard. Keep this, and remove the wildcards listed in the PROG-A4 rows. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Typed press identity** (clients.rs:33-48): ClientShellPressId separates physical keys, semantic keys and mouse buttons for release tracking, with a leak-free drain at teardown (clients.rs:370). [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Typed framing errors and size cap** (headless.rs:1567-1586): `FramingError::Oversized` is returned, not panicked on, and the cap is a parameter so tests can use small limits. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Bounded loop work** (headless.rs:87-90, 160-166, 341): a documented drain limit, a documented accept-poll interval with the reason for it, and a bounded server-event channel (64). [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Atomics with explicit ordering and cooperative cancel** (headless.rs:266-283, 453, 706-717): Acquire/Release on shared stop flags, and the accept thread polls the flag. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Typed loop events** (headless.rs:134-150): LoopEvent and RenderImpact with a doc comment saying why presentation is separate from delivery. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Fallible argv handling** (bootstrap.rs:24-30): missing arguments return InvalidInput instead of indexing. [audit-herdr-server-2.md]
- **Why-comments** (bootstrap.rs:237, handoff.rs:96-97, headless.rs:2992-2996): the comment records a constraint, not the code. [audit-herdr-server-2.md] Also: - discovery.rs ref-handling comments explain git semantics (packed-ref fallback) rather than restating code; no SLOP-1 hits in any audited file. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- Typed shutdown reason with structured logging: `ShutdownReason` enum with `info!(%reason, "server shutdown initiated")` (herdr/src/server/headless/lifecycle.rs:308-315) follows LOG-unstructured/LOG-level well. [audit-herdr-server-3.md]
- Structured tracing fields at decision points: `warn!(client_id, claimed, max, "trimming inline graphics assets from oversized pane surface")` (herdr/src/server/headless/render.rs:880-883). [audit-herdr-server-3.md]

- Explicit rollback function for pre-commit handoff failure with a commit point (herdr/src/server/headless/lifecycle.rs:276-288, 199-213): clear two-phase design, though it should be wrapped in a guard. [audit-herdr-server-3.md]
- Saturating counter arithmetic: `shell_projection_revision.saturating_add(1)` (herdr/src/server/headless/surface_interest.rs:23-24) states overflow behavior (RUST-HR-9). [audit-herdr-server-3.md]
- Checked conversions: `u16::try_from(...).ok()?` with `checked_add` in retained_surface.rs:33, 83, 141 rather than `as` casts. [audit-herdr-server-3.md]
- Bounded event drain with a limit constant and fairness tests: `drain_internal_events_with_forwarding_up_to(limit)` (herdr/src/server/headless/notifications.rs:730-747) plus herdr/src/server/headless/tests/event_fairness.rs asserting FIFO and leftover work. [audit-herdr-server-3.md]

- Env-mutating tests serialize on a shared config env lock (herdr/src/server/headless/tests/mod.rs:5008). [audit-herdr-server-4.md]
- Test names state the behavior under test (e.g. herdr/src/server/headless/tests/mod.rs:4992), and many comments explain why, not what (herdr/src/server/headless/tests/mod.rs:390). [audit-herdr-server-4.md]

- Opaque id newtype with a doc comment forbidding derivation from pane ids, plus `Borrow<str>` for `&str` map lookup (herdr/src/terminal/id.rs:6-11, :36-40). Add validation on Deserialize and a separator when adopting. [audit-herdr-terminal-1.md]
- Outcome enum instead of bool/Option for merge results: `UpwardMerge { Advanced, Unchanged, Unaligned }` (herdr/src/terminal/history_read.rs:40-44), consumed without wildcard arms. [audit-herdr-terminal-1.md]

- Monotonic sequence guarding of reports (`accept_hook_report` / `hook_report_is_newer`, 1742-1750, 1946) is a good protocol-level defense against reordered or replayed agent reports. [audit-herdr-terminal-2.md]
- Production code uses `saturating_duration_since` and `is_some_and`/`let-else` instead of unwrap (e.g. 300-301, 2207-2209); zero unwrap/expect/unsafe outside tests across 2451 lines. [audit-herdr-terminal-2.md]
- Typed `TerminalStateMutation` / `EffectiveStateChange` return values (96-122) report what changed instead of having callers diff state. [audit-herdr-terminal-2.md]
- Total function returning `Option` instead of panicking on empty or whitespace input, using `chars.next()?` (herdr/src/terminal/title.rs:10). [audit-herdr-terminal-3.md]
- Slicing by `first.len_utf8()` keeps multi-byte glyph handling UTF-8 safe with no byte-offset guessing (herdr/src/terminal/title.rs:11). [audit-herdr-terminal-3.md]
- Boundary-aware strip rule: a glyph is removed only if followed by whitespace or end, so `★task` is preserved (herdr/src/terminal/title.rs:14-15); tests pin this (title.rs:51-63). [audit-herdr-terminal-3.md]
- Unit tests sit beside the code, are table-driven, and cover Unicode and empty edge cases (herdr/src/terminal/title.rs:66-73). [audit-herdr-terminal-3.md]
- Small single-purpose module with no unsafe, unwrap, or `#[allow]`. [audit-herdr-terminal-3.md]
- **Three-state ref read instead of Option** - `RefFileRead { Content, Absent, Unavailable }` (herdr/src/workspace/git/discovery.rs:134) keeps "does not exist" distinct from "cannot be trusted", with the reason documented on the type. Adopt the same shape for PTY/socket/state-file probes. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Bounded reads of untrusted files** - `MAX_GIT_REF_FILE_BYTES` with `take(max + 1)` then a length check (herdr/src/workspace/git/discovery.rs:4, :169) detects over-limit rather than silently truncating. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Typed head identity** - `GitHeadIdentity { Branch{..}, Detached{..} }` (herdr/src/workspace/git/status.rs:65) makes detached-with-no-branch unrepresentable as a half-filled struct, and accessors match both variants exhaustively (:233). [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Dependency-stamped cache** - fingerprint plus file stamps with revalidation (`deps_current`, herdr/src/workspace/git/config.rs:26) and a negative-result retry window (herdr/src/workspace/git/status.rs:130). The design is sound; the tuple encoding is what to avoid. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Demand struct for refresh** - `GitStatusRefreshDemand` (herdr/src/workspace/git/status.rs:17) lets callers pay only for branch/ahead-behind work they need, matching the multiplicative-cost principle. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Exhaustive priority match** - `pane_attention_priority` matches every (state, seen) pair with no wildcard (herdr/src/workspace/aggregate.rs:50); only the u8 return type should change. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Pure state, no PTY needed** - Workspace aggregation takes `&HashMap<TerminalId, TerminalState>` (herdr/src/workspace/aggregate.rs:61) so it is unit-testable without runtimes. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Rollback on spawn failure** - split_pane_with_runtime closes the just-created layout node when the runtime fails to spawn and leaves focus/history untouched (herdr/src/workspace/tab.rs:397). [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Ownership-returning insert** - `insert_existing_pane` returns `Err(MovedPane)` so a failed move does not drop the pane state (herdr/src/workspace/tab.rs:488). [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Injectable seam for tests** - `read_config_with_user_paths` (herdr/src/workspace/git/config.rs:70) takes user config paths explicitly; extend this to HOME in the pattern helpers. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]
- **Behavioral test names and real asserts** - a scan of all #[test] fns in the audited files found none without an assert, and no sleeps or ignores. [audit-herdr-workspace.md]

- `TerminalKey` retains generated text, shifted codepoint, and native identity separately so consumers can distinguish typed text from physical key identity: `herdr/src/input/model.rs:79`. [audit-herdr-input]
- Input leases preserve the press/release lifecycle and explicitly distinguish consumed presses from forwarded ones: `herdr/src/input/lease.rs:21`. [audit-herdr-input]
- The parser rejects malformed protocol fields with `Option` propagation at its input boundary rather than panicking on malformed sequences: `herdr/src/input/parse.rs:28`. [audit-herdr-input]
- The indexed binding resolver uses an enum for direct versus prefix dispatch, keeping that distinction explicit: `herdr/src/input/keybindings.rs:9`. [audit-herdr-input]
- Mouse coordinate scaling uses widened integer arithmetic before bounding the result to the target dimensions: `herdr/src/input/mouse.rs:129`. [audit-herdr-input]
- Represent output as ordered `Bytes` and `Upload` operations, retaining raw upload data until output I/O (`herdr/src/kitty_graphics/output.rs:9-13`). [audit-herdr-kitty_graphics]
- Bound off-screen image retention by both count and decoded-byte budget (`herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:20-23`, `herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:883-891`). [audit-herdr-kitty_graphics]
- Use exhaustive format-to-format mapping for the controlled image-format enums (`herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:900-917`). [audit-herdr-kitty_graphics]
- Split oversized occluded images into visible grid pieces under a fixed per-frame crop budget, with a whole-image fallback (`herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:77-94`, `herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:146-165`). [audit-herdr-kitty_graphics]
- Keep tests adjacent to implementation and exercise ordering, cleanup, occlusion, and direct-asset replacement behavior (`herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:1178-1250`, `herdr/src/kitty_graphics/surface.rs:1535-1626`). [audit-herdr-kitty_graphics]
- Pane sizing is computed from the selected layout and chrome before a new terminal is started, avoiding a visible resize correction: `herdr/src/ui/panes.rs:81`. [audit-herdr-ui]
- UI geometry helpers are pure functions over `Rect` and explicit configuration, making layout behavior easy to test without a live terminal: `herdr/src/ui/sidebar.rs:30` and `herdr/src/ui/widgets.rs:15`. [audit-herdr-ui]
- Tab rendering consumes a `TabSurfaceView` containing an explicit target and precomputed pane geometry rather than reaching into mutable view caches: `herdr/src/ui/tab_surface.rs:119`. [audit-herdr-ui]
- Token configuration is resolved into a typed `ResolvedTokenKind` enum before rendering, separating configured token identity from display style: `herdr/src/ui/sidebar/tokens.rs:10`. [audit-herdr-ui]
- Text truncation uses terminal display width, including Unicode characters, rather than byte count: `herdr/src/ui/text.rs:3`. [audit-herdr-ui]
